CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this is

CausalStructures is an R package that binds to the Julia package CausalStructures.jl for representing, validating, and reasoning about causal graphs (DAG, UG, PDAG, CPDAG, MPDAG, ADMG, AG, MAG, PAG, UNKNOWN). CausalStructures.jl is compiled with juliac --trim=safe into a shared library by install_backend(), and every user-facing R function is a single .Call into that library — the actual algorithms live in the Julia package, not in this repo. There is no embedded Julia session at run time.

Common commands

# Build the compiled library for development (needs Julia >= 1.13 on the PATH).
# Do this once, and again after changing anything in inst/julia/; setup()
# prefers a build in inst/csjl over the one install_backend() makes.
julia --startup-file=no inst/julia/build.jl inst/csjl

# ... against a local CausalStructures.jl checkout instead of the release
CAUSALSTRUCTURES_JL_PATH=../CausalStructures.jl \
  julia --startup-file=no inst/julia/build.jl inst/csjl

# ... with the newest dependency versions [compat] allows, ignoring the manifest
julia --startup-file=no inst/julia/build.jl inst/csjl --update

# Update the shipped manifest (e.g. for a new CausalStructures.jl release);
# resolve with the Julia version the package requires, then rebuild and test
julia --startup-file=no --project=inst/julia -e 'import Pkg; Pkg.update()'

# Run the full test suite
Rscript -e 'pkgload::load_all("."); testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat")'

# Run a single test file
Rscript -e 'pkgload::load_all("."); testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-julia.R")'

# Regenerate roxygen docs (NAMESPACE + man/) after touching R/ or roxygen comments
Rscript -e 'roxygen2::roxygenise()'

# Full R CMD check. Installing does not build the library, so point the check
# at a build (as CI does), or the tests and examples needing it are skipped.
CAUSALSTRUCTURES_LIBRARY=$PWD/inst/csjl/csjl.so Rscript -e 'devtools::check()'

# Re-knit README.md from README.Rmd after editing README.Rmd
Rscript -e 'devtools::build_readme()'

# Build pkgdown site locally
Rscript -e 'pkgdown::build_site(devel = TRUE)'

Tests that need the compiled library call skip_if_no_julia() (see tests/testthat/helper-julia.R) and are skipped otherwise. julia_ready() checks that the library loads.

Pre-commit hooks (.pre-commit-config.yaml) enforce: air formatting, jarl/panache linting, README.md being newer than README.Rmd, and roxygen docs being up to date (roxygen2::needs_roxygenize() must be FALSE) — run roxygen2::roxygenise() before committing if you touched R/, DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, or man/.

Architecture

Building the library (install_backend(), inst/julia/)

  • Installing the package builds nothing, so it installs (and passes CRAN’s checks) without Julia; then every function errors, julia_ready() is FALSE, and examples and tests skip. CRAN’s policy forbids downloading software and writing to the home directory (~/.julia) during installation, which an install-time build needs; a function the user calls explicitly may.
  • install_backend() (R/install.R) finds Julia (julia argument, $JULIA, else julia on the PATH), requires >= 1.13, asks for confirmation when interactive, and runs the installed package’s julia/build.jl in a child process. It writes csjl.so (.dylib on macOS, .dll on Windows) to tools::R_user_dir("CausalStructures", "data")/csjl/<package version>/, so a library built for another version (whose entrypoints may not match src/entrypoints.h) is never loaded; other versions’ directories are pruned. It builds into a temporary sibling directory and renames it into place (a loaded DLL cannot be deleted on Windows but can be renamed), then loads it with setup(), unless a library is already loaded: Julia can only start once per process, so a rebuild is used from the next session.
  • setup() looks for the library in CAUSALSTRUCTURES_LIBRARY, then system.file("csjl") (a development build in inst/csjl), then the install_backend() directory. CI builds with build.jl directly and sets CAUSALSTRUCTURES_LIBRARY.
  • inst/julia/build.jl mirrors CausalStructures.jl’s own trim-check: it instantiates the binding project (inst/julia/Project.toml, CausalStructures from the General registry, or CAUSALSTRUCTURES_JL_PATH via Pkg.develop) in a scratch copy, then compiles it from a separate temporary environment (so JuliaC is never compiled into the library) with JuliaC’s recipe API: the equivalent of --output-lib --trim=safe --experimental --compile-ccallable, plus the C source set_threads.c, which the JuliaC CLI cannot add.
  • inst/julia/Manifest.toml is committed and shipped, so a package version always builds against the dependency versions it was tested with: under --trim=safe, a dependency release that adds a dynamic call would otherwise break every user’s build at once. install_backend(update = TRUE) (--update) resolves the newest versions [compat] allows instead, and install_backend(project = dir) (--project=dir) builds from a user’s own Project.toml/Manifest.toml (same name, UUID and deps; e.g. a [sources] entry for a development CausalStructures.jl). If the manifest fails to instantiate (resolved with another Julia version), build.jl warns and resolves from [compat]. Copies are chmoded writable, since an installed package’s files may be read-only.
  • The library links against the runtime of the Julia that built it (its RUNPATH points there), so nothing is bundled. If that Julia is removed (e.g. by a juliaup update), loading fails and setup() tells the user to run install_backend(force = TRUE).
  • install_backend() unsets LD_LIBRARY_PATH for the build: R puts its own library directories on it, which otherwise makes Julia’s bundled tools (Pkg’s zstd) load the system libraries instead of Julia’s.
  • A juliac library fixes its Julia options when compiled (one thread, Julia signal handling off) and ignores JULIA_NUM_THREADS (JuliaC.jl#152). set_threads.c (adapted from Ribasim) exports csjl_set_julia_threads, which sets jl_options before Julia initializes; setup() calls it through the shim’s C_csjl_set_threads after dyn.load() and before the first entrypoint, from JULIA_NUM_THREADS (a count or "auto"). More than one thread turns on Julia’s signal handling, which multi-threaded GC needs.
  • inst/csjl/ is development build output: gitignored and in .Rbuildignore.
  • Windows: a DLL has no RUNPATH, so build.jl records Julia’s Sys.BINDIR in julia_bindir next to csjl.dll and setup() prepends it to the PATH before dyn.load(). A ccall without a library only searches Julia’s own DLLs on Windows, so rapi.jl names every R symbol with @R(sym), which adds "R.dll" there (and @r_global(sym) for R’s global SEXPs).

The binding layer (inst/julia/src/)

This is the code to read first for anything touching the R<->Julia boundary.

  • rapi.jl is generic: Julia calls R’s C API directly (the library is loaded into the R process, so ccall(:Rf_allocVector, ...) etc. resolve against libR). It holds the from_sexp/to_sexp conversions, graphs as external pointers (GraphHandle), the csjl_error error object, a preserved cache of R strings per node name, and the @rcall macro.
  • @rcall f(a::T, ...)::R exports csjl_r_f(a::SEXP, ...)::SEXP: it converts each argument with from_sexp(T, a), calls f, and converts the result. A return type of GraphHandle/Vector{GraphHandle} makes the result a new cgraph (or a list of them); SEXP passes an R object built in place through unchanged (edges, edge_marks, simulate_data).
  • Errors never unwind through Julia frames: a Julia exception is caught in the entrypoint and returned as a character vector with class csjl_error, which the shim in src/ raises. _error_message only reads the message of the exception types CausalStructures throws, since rendering an arbitrary exception is a dynamic call --trim rejects. R itself only longjmps out of allocations, i.e. when out of memory.
  • csjl.jl is CausalStructures-specific: a registry of graphs keyed by an integer handle, and one function plus one @rcall declaration per exported R function. Graph functions take h::Int64 and branch on the concrete class with @on "name" g (DAG, ADMG) body (or ALL), because a graph read from the registry is only known as CausalGraph and --trim rejects the dynamic dispatch. List only the classes the CausalStructures.jl function has methods for; other classes get a clean “not supported for a ” error.
  • --trim=safe pitfalls already hit here: splatting a vector into varargs (use _fold), nameof(typeof(g)) on an abstract graph (use _class_name), more than two Union{T,Nothing} arguments in one call (take raw SEXP and convert inside, as generate_graph does), and a type passed as a keyword argument (class = T, inlined with @inline in _generate).
  • Adding a wrapped function: write the Julia function in csjl.jl, add an @rcall declaration, add CSJL_ENTRY(name, nargs) to src/entrypoints.h, and call it from the R wrapper as .Call(C_name, ...). Then rebuild the library (and reload, which recompiles src/). A wrong nargs shows up as R’s “Incorrect number of arguments” error on the first call.

The registration shim (src/)

  • The package has its own small shared object, CausalStructures.so, loaded by useDynLib(CausalStructures, .registration = TRUE, .fixes = "C_"). src/init.c registers one .Call routine per line of src/entrypoints.h (an X-macro list), each forwarding to the library’s csjl_r_<name> through a function pointer, plus csjl_bind and csjl_set_threads. A routine raises a returned csjl_error as an R error itself, once the Julia call has returned, so no R wrapper needs to check results.
  • The csjl library cannot be linked into it (it is built by install_backend() against the user’s Julia and loaded later by setup()), so csjl_bind resolves every pointer with R_FindSymbol once the library is loaded. A routine called before that raises an error instead of crashing.
  • This keeps every .Call in R/ a registered routine of the package itself, so R CMD check’s foreign-function checks pass without workarounds.

The R side (R/session.R)

  • setup() (also run from .onLoad) dyn.load()s the library, sets the Julia thread count (see above), and binds the shim’s routines to it (.Call(C_csjl_bind, ...)). Exported functions are a direct .Call(C_name, ...). The library path can be overridden with CAUSALSTRUCTURES_LIBRARY.
  • Calls are microsecond-scale, so R-side overhead matters: avoid extra wrapper layers on the hot path, and match.arg() (about 3.5 µs) is skipped when the argument is missing (x <- if (missing(x)) x[[1L]] else match.arg(x)).
  • Node sets go in and come out as character vectors. Results with no set come back as NULL; nested results (all_backdoor_sets(), possible_joint_parent_sets(), …) come back as R lists built library-side.

The edge-operator DSL (R/dsl.R, R/construction.R)

cgraph(A %-->% X + Y, X %-->% M %-->% Y) uses custom infix operators (%-->%, %<--%, %---%, %<->%, %o->%, etc., listed in .edge_glyphs) that are never evaluated — ... is captured unevaluated and walked as an unevaluated call tree (.is_edge_call, .is_node_expr, .contains_edge), then translated into CausalStructures.jl’s own string DSL (e.g. "A --> X + Y, X --> M --> Y"). cgraph(spec = "...") bypasses the operator DSL entirely for programmatic construction from a spec string built at runtime. Note the custom-operator precedence gotcha documented at the top of dsl.R: %any% operators bind tighter than +, so A %-->% B + C parses as (A %-->% B) + C.

Graph objects

A causal graph is an R external pointer with S3 class "cgraph", created by the library: its address is the graph’s registry handle, and a C finalizer releases the library’s copy when R collects it (the release is deferred to the next graph store, since a finalizer can run mid-call). Query functions (R/queries.R, R/identification.R) return plain R vectors, lists and data frames; transform functions (R/transform.R) return new cgraphs. R/data.R covers simulating data from a graph.

Plotting (R/plot.R, R/plot-options.R, R/plot-routing.R, R/layout.R)

  • cgraph_layout() (R/layout.R) computes node positions. "sugiyama" is the library’s sugiyama_layout entrypoint, which calls Sugiyama.jl directly on the adjacency matrix (every edge as src -> dst, so any class works) rather than through CausalStructures.jl’s layout(), whose Val(method) dispatch and forwarded kwargs... --trim rejects. plot() uses the sugiyama_paths entrypoint instead (Sugiyama.jl’s sugiyama_paths), which also returns each edge’s route through its bend points, drawn as an explicit edge path as in CausalStructures.jl; node pairs with parallel edges get no route, so they still fan out. "stress", "shell" and "squaregrid" are plain R: NetworkLayout.jl does not compile under --trim, and causal graphs are small enough that dense-matrix R code is fast. Stress starts from classical MDS (stats::cmdscale()), so it needs no RNG and is deterministic.
  • The grid-graphics rendering (plot.cgraph() in R/plot.R, edge routing in R/plot-routing.R) is adapted from caugi ’s plotting code (see attribution comments in those files and inst/COPYRIGHTS) rather than written from scratch — check there before assuming rendering behavior is bespoke to this package.
  • plot_options()/plot_default_options() (R/plot-options.R) is a dedicated get/set/reset accessor for plot styling defaults (node_style, edge_style, label_style, title_style), deliberately kept separate from base options() since it’s a nested graphics-parameter list rather than a flat behavioral toggle.

Warmup (R/warmup.R)

warmup() calls every exported wrapper once on small graphs. The library is compiled ahead of time, so there is no JIT to warm up; it now serves as a quick smoke test of the whole API.

File organization

DESCRIPTION’s Collate: field defines load order (session.R first); keep new files added to R/ there if load order matters.
